defect_observations.observation: The regular-conditional-laws annex concludes 'lambda-system' after checking closure under complements and countable disjoint unions (lines 106-110 and 120-124; also 213-217 and 283-288). def:p15-pi-lambda (measurable-probability.tex 400-408) and Durrett app. A.1 p. 456 define a lambda-system by nested differences and increasing unions, and thm:p15-measure-uniqueness is proved for that definition. The two-line bridge (B minus A is the complement of the disjoint union of B^c and A; an increasing union is a disjoint union of increments) is not written. Other P15 annexes verify the official conditions explicitly (product-measures annex 159-163, measure-extension annex 250-260, independent-random-variables annex 125-136). Rigor elision; not counted as a coverage gap.

The uniqueness step asserts that the sets phi^{-1}(E cap (-inf,q]), q rational, together with S, form a countable generating pi-system for the target sigma-algebra (also lines 232-236). Generation follows from thm:p15-measurability-criterion applied to phi as a real-valued map, thm:p15-borel-generators, and S = phi^{-1}(trace Borel sigma-algebra) for a measurable isomorphism, but that derivation is not written.

Measurability of the continuous maps psi|_S and R between metric subspaces carrying trace Borel sigma-algebras is used (K = R^{-1}(S) Borel in C; phi measurable; R o D measurable) without proof. The handbook proves continuous-implies-Borel only between Euclidean spaces (thm:p15-measurable-operations, measurable-probability.tex 291-300). The step follows from the generator criterion in two lines but is not written.

'both are generated by intersections of Borel rectangles with E^(n)' relies on the trace-generation identity (the trace of sigma(C) equals the sigma-algebra generated by the traces), which is not proved anywhere in the handbook. Only the easy inclusion (product sigma-algebra on E^(n) contained in the trace Borel sigma-algebra) is used by the later steps, so the argument stands.
The countable basis of finite-coordinate rational interval conditions is asserted without the rational-approximation step; the Euclidean analogue is written at measurable-probability annex 149-157.

The proof reuses earlier arguments by reference ('apply to H_q(Y)', 'The fully proved CDF argument', 'calculations from the real-law proof', 'The same Borel-image and transport arguments as above'). The referenced steps are written at annex 49-125 and 151-170 and apply verbatim with (Omega, G) replaced by (T, T). Accepted as written steps; recorded for transparency.

Durrett p. 214 (continuation of Example 4.1.6) assumes a strictly positive joint density and uses the ratio with no default. The handbook theorem takes f >= 0 with an explicit exceptional set D^c and a default point mass. The source case is included, but the entry does not name the source's positivity hypothesis or its locus.

Durrett's 'nice' (p. 53) requires only a 1-1 map into R that is measurable in both directions, with no Borel-image requirement; the handbook's 'standard Borel' requires a Borel image. The handbook says it makes the image requirement explicit (regular-conditional-laws.tex 108-109) but does not state outright that its existence theorems cover the source's nice spaces only when the image is Borel.
